newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Gazprom bank unit AEB sees '96,'97 profit.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom bank unit AEB sees '96,'97 profit.

text.p: Altalanos Ertekforgalmi Bank Rt (AEB), the Hungarian subsidiary of the Russian gas firm RAO Gazprom's banking arm, made a slight profit in 1996 and expects to increase it tenfold in 1997, the bank's chairman said on Tuesday.

"The board of directors has accepted the bank's 1996 preliminary report, under which it made an after-tax profit of 134 million forints compared to a significant loss in 1995," Mikhail Nikolayevich Rakhimulov told a news conference. "In 1997, we expect our profit to be 10 times that much."

In 1995, AEB had a loss accrued to the balance sheet of 635 million forints and assets of 38.0 billion forints. By the end of November, 1996, AEB's assets increased to 60.1 billion, according to a statement.
Gazprombank acquired AEB from Hungary's state privatisation agency APV Rt and from the North American Central European Development Corp last August.
AEB is Gazprombank's only foreign subsidiary and the Russian institution intends to significantly increase the bank's size, making it its base for Central-Eastern Europe, Rakhimulov said.
"Last year, AEB was the 34th biggest commercial bank in Hungary (out of 46)," he said. "By 1998, we hope to make it one of the top five."

As part of the changes, Gazprombank will double AEB's shareholders' equity to 10 billion forints as soon as the Russian central bank approves the deal, and obtain a total of $250 million from loans and from a bond issue, to finance gas-related investments in eastern Europe, he said.
In addition, AEB will open new branches, continue to shed its smaller retail customers and will finance the development of a new gas pipeline to Eastern Europe, Rakhimulov said.

It was announced last year that Gazprom, the Hungarian oil and gas company MOL and their joint venture Panrusgaz were negotiating about the construction of the pipeline, which is expected to supply Hungary, Slovakia, Slovenia and Italy with Russian gas.
